iterations.theme: Analiza riječkog kurikuluma zdravstvenog odgoja, biološki temelji kritike i osnivanje udruge Članak 64

sections.subtitle: Prva žena gošća podcasta: doktorica znanosti, supruga i majka
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pozdravlja Josipu Nemet u studiju i predstavlja je kao prvu ženu gošću podcasta
sections.content:
Epizoda počinje isječkom u kojem gošća oštro ocjenjuje stanje struke koja bi se trebala brinuti o čovjeku. **Josipa Nemet**, doktorica znanosti, kaže da je moderna psihologija u posljednjih dvadesetak do trideset godina "nanijela jako puno štete" i da se degradirala jer je zanemarila biologiju. Prema njezinim riječima, ta struka zaboravlja da se bavi čovjekom "koji nije od jučer", čovjekom "čije tijelo je drevno".

Nakon pozdrava "Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip" voditelj podcasta *Redefinicija* predstavlja gošću kao suprugu, majku i doktoricu znanosti koja ima "jednu jako važnu priču". Pita je i kako se osjeća kao prva žena koja gostuje u emisiji.

Josipa Nemet odgovara da za taj podatak nije znala. Kaže da joj je drago i da joj je čast te zahvaljuje voditeljima što se zanimaju za teme važne za djecu i roditelje. Gostovanje vidi i kao podršku radu koji ona i njezini suradnici obavljaju u društvu.
sections.subtitle_en: The first female guest of the podcast: doctor of science, wife and mother
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host greets Josipa Nemet in the studio and introduces her as the first female guest of the podcast
sections.content_en:
The episode begins with an excerpt in which the guest sharply assesses the state of the profession that should be caring for man. **Josipa Nemet**, doctor of science, says that modern psychology in the last twenty to thirty years has "caused a great deal of damage" and that it has degraded itself because it neglected biology. According to her words, that profession forgets that it deals with man "who is not from yesterday", man "whose body is ancient".

After the greeting "Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph", the host of the *Redefinicija* podcast introduces the guest as a wife, mother, and doctor of science who has "a very important story". He also asks her how she feels as the first woman to guest on the show.

Josipa Nemet replies that she did not know that fact. She says that she is glad and that it is an honor, and thanks the hosts for being interested in topics important to children and parents. She also sees the guest appearance as support for the work that she and her collaborators carry out in society.

sections.subtitle: Kako je riječki kurikulum ušao u škole kroz "rupu u zakonu"
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet objašnjava kako je kurikulum zdravstvenog odgoja ušao u riječke škole kao izvannastavna aktivnost
sections.content:
Glavna tema razgovora je analiza kurikuluma zdravstvenog odgoja koju je Josipa Nemet napravila sa suradnicima. Ona objašnjava da je program prošle godine bio u pilot fazi u Rijeci, a ove se godine provodi u gotovo svim riječkim školama. Zasad se izvodi kao **izvannastavna aktivnost**.

Prema njezinim riječima, kurikulum je u škole ušao kroz "rupu u zakonu". Ta je mogućnost bila predviđena za projekte poput paške čipke te glazbenih i plesnih aktivnosti, kojima udruge popunjavaju dio dječjeg vremena. Grad Rijeka iskoristio ju je za uvođenje vlastite verzije zdravstvenog odgoja.

Gošća naglašava da takav program nije bio potreban jer nacionalni kurikulum već ima **međupredmetnu temu Zdravlje**. Ona pokriva i spolno zdravlje, pa učenici u osmom razredu uče o vrstama kontracepcije. I taj sadržaj smatra "vrlo diskutabilnim". Gradskoj vlasti to ipak nije bilo dovoljno. Josipa Nemet tvrdi da se ona ugledala na inozemne istomišljenike koji su društvenim aktivizmom svoje programe uveli u nacionalne kurikulume. Rezultat je, kaže, "vrlo loš i štetan kurikulum" u koji su "infiltrirane i određene stavke rodne ideologije".
sections.subtitle_en: How the Rijeka curriculum entered schools through a "legal loophole"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet explains how the health education curriculum entered Rijeka schools as an extracurricular activity
sections.content_en:
The main topic of the conversation is an analysis of the health education curriculum that Josipa Nemet conducted with associates. She explains that the program was in a pilot phase in Rijeka last year, and this year it is being implemented in almost all Rijeka schools. For now, it is being carried out as an **extracurricular activity**.

According to her words, the curriculum entered schools through a "legal loophole". That possibility was intended for projects such as Pag lace and music and dance activities, with which associations fill part of children's time. The City of Rijeka used it to introduce its own version of health education.

The guest emphasizes that such a program was not necessary because the national curriculum already has the **cross-curricular topic Health**. It also covers sexual health, so eighth-grade students learn about types of contraception. She also considers that content "very debatable". Nevertheless, that was not enough for the city administration. Josipa Nemet claims that it modeled itself after foreign like-minded individuals who, through social activism, introduced their programs into national curriculums. The result, she says, is a "very bad and harmful curriculum" into which "certain items of gender ideology have also been infiltrated".

sections.subtitle: Od majčinske stanke do znanstvene i pravne analize
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća opisuje kako se uključila u borbu nakon što joj je sin krenuo u vrtić
sections.content:
Josipa Nemet otkriva i osobni razlog uključivanja. Neko je vrijeme bila u "fazi mirovanja" i nije bila društveno aktivna jer je bila kod kuće sa sinom. Kad je sin na jesen krenuo u vrtić, dobila je prostor za angažman.

Na to ju je potaknula moralna obveza, ali i struka, jer dolazi iz znanstvenog miljea. Odlučila se suprotstaviti programu koji ideološki aktivisti, kako kaže, predstavljaju kao znanstveni odgoj. Po njezinu mišljenju on "nema nikakve veze sa znanošću" i nema uporište u neurorazvojnoj znanosti ni u pedagogiji.

Okupila se šira skupina ljudi koja je odlučila javno progovoriti:
- roditelji,
- ljudi koji vole djecu, ali svoje nemaju,
- učitelji,
- pravnici.

Prvi im je cilj bio pokazati javnosti što kurikulum sadrži. Josipa Nemet ga je detaljno analizirala i s pravnog stajališta. Tvrdi da se njime posredno krše pojedini zakoni, među njima i odredbe Kaznenog zakona o pristanku djeteta na spolni odnos. Smatra da se roditeljima uskraćuje i pravo na **informirani pristanak**. Roditelji koji su pristali na pilot projekt i ovogodišnje sudjelovanje, prema njezinim riječima, nisu bili propisno informirani o sadržaju programa.
sections.subtitle_en: From a maternal break to scientific and legal analysis
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes how she got involved in the fight after her son started kindergarten
sections.content_en:
Josipa Nemet also reveals a personal reason for getting involved. For some time, she was in a "dormant phase" and was not socially active because she was at home with her son. When her son started kindergarten in the fall, she gained room for engagement.

She was prompted to do so by a moral obligation, but also by her profession, because she comes from a scientific milieu. She decided to oppose a program that ideological activists, as she says, present as scientific education. In her opinion, it "has nothing to do with science" and has no foothold in neurodevelopmental science nor in pedagogy.

A broader group of people gathered who decided to speak out publicly:
- parents,
- people who love children, but do not have their own,
- teachers,
- lawyers.

Their first goal was to show the public what the curriculum contains. Josipa Nemet analyzed it in detail from a legal standpoint as well. She claims that it indirectly violates certain laws, among them the provisions of the Criminal Code on a child's consent to sexual intercourse. She considers that parents are also denied the right to **informed consent**. Parents who agreed to the pilot project and this year's participation, according to her words, were not properly informed about the content of the program.

sections.subtitle: Rodna ideologija i "epistemološka zbunjenost" djece
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet govori o dovođenju djece u stanje epistemološke zbunjenosti
sections.content:
Prvi problematični dio kurikuluma koji gošća izdvaja jest rodna ideologija. Djecu se, tvrdi, dovodi u stanje **epistemološke zbunjenosti**. Sugerira im se da njihov dojam, mišljenje i samoodređenje vrijede više od objektivne istine.

Zbog toga djeca dobivaju, kako kaže, "neprimjerenu autonomiju nad objektivnom istinom", a za nju još nisu sposobna zbog stupnja neurobiološkog razvoja. Pojmovi se miješaju, pa se dijete uvjerava da njegov spol može biti jednak rodu, da može biti različit od roda ili da može biti "nikakav".
sections.subtitle_en: Gender ideology and "epistemological confusion" of children
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet speaks about bringing children into a state of epistemological confusion
sections.content_en:
The first problematic part of the curriculum that the guest singles out is gender ideology. Children, she claims, are being brought into a state of **epistemological confusion**. It is suggested to them that their impression, opinion, and self-determination are worth more than objective truth.

Because of this, children receive, as she says, "inappropriate autonomy over objective truth," and they are not yet capable of it due to their stage of neurobiological development. Concepts are mixed up, so the child is convinced that their sex can be equal to gender, that it can be different from gender, or that it can be "none".

sections.subtitle: Spolni užitak u prvom planu i dječji dopaminski sustav
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava kako kurikulum cilja na dječji nagradni sustav u mozgu
sections.content:
Josipa Nemet kao posebno osjetljivo područje navodi spolnost. Kaže da kurikulum snažno ističe **spolni užitak** i da je spolnost "amputirana" od svoje glavne, biološke svrhe, a to je reprodukcija. U udžbenicima i ishodima kurikuluma reprodukcija se, prema njezinim riječima, tretira kao nešto suvišno, a naglasak je na djetetovu pravu na užitak.

Naglašavanje užitka po njoj posredno cilja na osjetljivost djetetova **nagradnog sustava u mozgu**, odnosno dopaminskog sustava. Objašnjava da je to jedini sustav koji je kod djeteta zaista razvijen. Kurikulum dijete gura da se njime koristi, a izostaje socijalna modulacija, odnosno vođenje od strane okoline. Djetetu se kaže "ti možeš sam izabrati", iako ono to još ne može.

Prema njezinu objašnjenju, djetetu nedostaju **regulatorne sinapse**. One omogućuju da procijeni posljedice svog ponašanja, da planira i da nagone uskladi s moralnim načelima zajednice, društvenim normama i vlastitim iskustvima. Kurikulum ga ipak, ističe gošća, uporno uvjerava da je ono to koje ima pravo pristati.
sections.subtitle_en: Sexual pleasure in the foreground and the child's dopamine system
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains how the curriculum targets the child's reward system in the brain
sections.content_en:
Josipa Nemet cites sexuality as a particularly sensitive area. She says that the curriculum strongly emphasizes **sexual pleasure** and that sexuality is "amputated" from its main, biological purpose, which is reproduction. In textbooks and curriculum outcomes, reproduction is, according to her words, treated as something superfluous, while the emphasis is on the child's right to pleasure.

According to her, emphasizing pleasure indirectly targets the sensitivity of the child's **reward system in the brain**, that is, the dopamine system. She explains that this is the only system that is truly developed in a child. The curriculum pushes the child to use it, while social modulation, that is, guidance by the environment, is absent. The child is told "you can choose for yourself," even though it cannot do so yet.

According to her explanation, the child lacks **regulatory synapses**. They enable evaluating the consequences of one's behavior, planning, and aligning impulses with the moral principles of the community, social norms, and one's own experiences. The curriculum, however, the guest emphasizes, persistently convinces it that it is the one who has the right to consent.

sections.subtitle: Zašto je pojam "pristanka" za djecu sporan
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet objašnjava problematiku pojma pristanka u kontekstu djece
sections.content:
Gošća posebno kritizira termin **pristanka**. Tvrdi da je on "duboko ukorijenjen u pedofilskom narativu prema djeci". U toj se retorici inzistira na tome da dijete ima pravo pristati, a ako pristane, "sve je dozvoljeno".

Josipa Nemet podsjeća da su društvo i pravo dosad dijete smatrali razvojno izrazito osjetljivim bićem. Zato mu se do 18. godine ne dopušta kupnja cigareta ili alkohola ni vožnja automobila. Javni i pravni život, kaže, prepoznaje da dijete ne može donositi dobre i slobodne odluke za sebe pa umjesto njega odlučuje zajednica. Kurikulum, po njezinu mišljenju, uvodi iznimku samo za spolnost i sugerira da dijete može ravnopravno sudjelovati u spolnom životu iako još nije spolno zrelo.

Pojašnjava da pod spolnom zrelošću ne misli samo na tijelo. Spolno sazrijeva i dječji mozak, u kojem se nalaze "tisuće i tisuće" receptora za spolne hormone.
sections.subtitle_en: Why the concept of "consent" for children is contentious
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet explains the issue of the concept of consent in the context of children
sections.content_en:
The guest particularly criticizes the term **consent**. She claims that it is "deeply rooted in the pedophile narrative toward children". In that rhetoric, it is insisted that a child has the right to consent, and if it consents, "everything is permitted".

Josipa Nemet reminds that society and the law have until now considered a child to be a developmentally extremely sensitive being. That is why, until the age of 18, it is not permitted to purchase cigarettes or alcohol, nor to drive a car. Public and legal life, she says, recognizes that a child cannot make good and free decisions for itself, so the community decides instead. The curriculum, in her opinion, introduces an exception only for sexuality and suggests that a child can equally participate in sexual life even though it is not yet sexually mature.

She clarifies that by sexual maturity she does not mean only the body. The child's brain also matures sexually, in which there are "thousands and thousands" of receptors for sex hormones.

sections.subtitle: Bez modela odgode, kontracepcija obrađena površno
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o izostanku modela odgode i štetnim učincima kontracepcije koji se ne spominju
sections.content:
Josipa Nemet kritizira i obradu zaštite. Kaže da kurikulum potpuno zaobilazi model koji smatra najuspješnijim i najzdravijim za djecu: **odgodu do sposobnosti za trajnu i vjernu vezu**. Taj stav, ističe, ne zastupa samo iz svjetonazorskih razloga nego i iz pozicije biologije. Prema njezinu objašnjenju, sustav vezivanja razvio se kod čovjeka jer je odrastanje ljudskog mladunčeta zahtjevno i traži dugotrajno ulaganje. Zato je najbolji model onaj u kojem su majka i otac trajno i vjerno povezani.

Kontracepcija se u kurikulumu, kaže, obrađuje površno, samo nabrajanjem metoda. Prvi se put spominje i takozvana **urgentna kontracepcija**, koje nema u međupredmetnoj temi Zdravlje. Gošća tvrdi da je riječ o abortivnom sredstvu, a ne o kontracepciji.

Najvećim problemom, prisutnim i u nacionalnom kurikulumu, smatra to što se ne navode štetni učinci kontraceptivnih sredstava. Ako se već inzistira na informiranju djece, kaže, treba ih informirati potpuno. Iako je to tabu tema i teško je dobiti projekt za takva istraživanja, navodi da danas postoje desetci radova o štetnim posljedicama. Spominje:
- srčane i moždane udare,
- smanjenje gustoće kostiju,
- upale i trajnu neplodnost kod spirale,
- neplodnost nakon dugotrajne upotrebe hormonske kontracepcije.

Gošća dodaje da djetetu informacija sama po sebi malo znači. U emotivnoj i "dopaminski nabijenoj" situaciji ono se oslanja na limbički sustav, koji traži trenutnu nagradu. Inhibicijske sinapse koje bi mu rekle "Stani, čekaj, usporedi, pa odluči" još nisu razvijene. Zato je, kaže, kod djeteta najvažnije izgraditi osjećaj vanjske norme. Pritom ne misli na sram nego na svijest da je nešto za njega ne samo trenutno nego i trajno štetno. Kao veliki propust navodi i izostanak teme pornografije, koju opisuje kao najrašireniju i najozbiljniju bihevioralnu ovisnost današnjice.
sections.subtitle_en: Without the delay model, contraception treated superficially
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the absence of the delay model and the harmful effects of contraception that are not mentioned
sections.content_en:
Josipa Nemet also criticizes the treatment of protection. She says that the curriculum completely bypasses the model she considers the most successful and healthiest for children: **delay until the ability for a lasting and faithful relationship**. That stance, she emphasizes, she advocates not only for worldview reasons but also from the position of biology. According to her explanation, the bonding system developed in humans because the upbringing of a human young is demanding and requires long-term investment. That is why the best model is the one in which the mother and father are permanently and faithfully connected.

Contraception in the curriculum, she says, is treated superficially, only by enumerating methods. For the first time, so-called **emergency contraception** is also mentioned, which is not present in the cross-curricular topic Health. The guest claims that this is an abortifacient agent, and not contraception.

She considers the biggest problem, present also in the national curriculum, to be that the harmful effects of contraceptive agents are not stated. If there is already insistence on informing children, she says, they should be informed completely. Although this is a taboo topic and it is difficult to obtain a project for such research, she states that today there are dozens of papers on harmful consequences. She mentions:
- heart attacks and strokes,
- reduction of bone density,
- inflammations and permanent infertility with the IUD,
- infertility after long-term use of hormonal contraception.

The guest adds that information in itself means little to a child. In an emotional and "dopamine-charged" situation, it relies on the limbic system, which seeks an immediate reward. The inhibitory synapses that would tell it "Stop, wait, compare, and then decide" are not yet developed. That is why, she says, the most important thing with a child is to build a sense of an external norm. By that, she does not mean shame, but rather the awareness that something is for it not only currently, but also permanently harmful. As a major omission, she also cites the absence of the topic of pornography, which she describes as the most widespread and most serious behavioral addiction of today.

sections.subtitle: Pobačaj kao "rješenje", a roditelji izvan jednadžbe
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj i gošća razgovaraju o tome kako kurikulum predstavlja pobačaj i zaobilazi roditelje
sections.content:
Voditelja zanima kako kurikulum pristupa pobačaju. Josipa Nemet potvrđuje da se pobačaj navodi kao jedno od rješenja u slučaju neželjene trudnoće. Ni u jednom trenutku se, kaže, ne spominje da se time nekom biću oduzima život.

Jednako problematičnim smatra to što se nigdje ne spominje **savjetovanje s roditeljima**. Kad se mlade upućuje da potraže pomoć ako im nije dobro, uvijek ih se usmjerava stručnjacima. Roditelji se ne spominju kao osobe koje mogu pomoći u izazovnoj situaciji, pri ozbiljnoj odluci ili u emocionalno nestabilnom stanju.

Voditelj zaključuje da su roditelji "izvan svake jednadžbe", a gošća se s tim slaže. On dodaje da takav zdravstveni odgoj vidi kao vrstu **ideološkog preodgoja** koji nameće ranu seksualizaciju, a kao neizravnu posljedicu ima raspad društva.
sections.subtitle_en: Abortion as a "solution", and parents outside the equation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host and the guest discuss how the curriculum presents abortion and bypasses parents
sections.content_en:
The host is interested in how the curriculum approaches abortion. Josipa Nemet confirms that abortion is cited as one of the solutions in the case of an unwanted pregnancy. At no point, she says, is it mentioned that this takes away the life of a being.

She considers it equally problematic that **consultation with parents** is nowhere mentioned. When young people are directed to seek help if they are not well, they are always directed to specialists. Parents are not mentioned as persons who can help in a challenging situation, with a serious decision, or in an emotionally unstable state.

The host concludes that parents are "outside of every equation", and the guest agrees with this. He adds that he sees such health education as a kind of **ideological re-education** that imposes early sexualization, and has the breakdown of society as an indirect consequence.

sections.subtitle: Rascjep spolnosti i reprodukcije kao presedan u biološkoj povijesti
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet kao biologinja govori o rascjepu spolnosti od reprodukcije
sections.content:
Josipa Nemet nastavlja na voditeljevu misao: društvo se najlakše mijenja preko djece, odnosno preko normi koje se upisuju u njihovu neurobiologiju, osobito kroz spolni moral. Sadašnje stanje vidi kao neizbježnu posljedicu "ogromnog rascjepa" koji se dogodio prije pedesetak godina.

Kao biologinja taj rascjep naziva **presedanom** u 4,5 milijardi godina dugoj povijesti života. Pojavilo se, kaže, biće koje smatra da se nije dobro razmnožavati, a na kraju i biće koje više ne misli da je dobro živjeti. Ilustrira to primjerom: stanice nemaju svijest, ali se uvijek bore za život. I kod osobe koja si pokušava oduzeti život, kaže, "sve njegove stanice se s njim ne slažu". Time objašnjava velik broj neuspjelih pokušaja samoubojstva.

Biologija, objašnjava, teži preživljavanju do razmnožavanja. Čovjek kao svjesno biće uz to ima i višu dimenziju: slobodno se odlučuje voljeti drugu osobu. Ipak, obrasci su duboko upisani u tijelo. Odnos muškog i ženskog opisuje kao "jako finu i osjetljivu regulaciju ravnoteže". Muške i ženske gamete postoje gotovo dvije milijarde godina i uvijek su koevoluirale, pa je svaka promjena kod jednog spola tražila komplementarnu promjenu kod drugog. Sve te promjene vodile su zajedništvu i stvaranju života.

Nasuprot toj povijesti stoji "jadnih 50 godina", na koje se biologija ne može prilagoditi. Najprije je spolnost odvojena od reprodukcije, a zatim i užitak, koji je evolucijski mlađi, star oko petsto milijuna godina, a nastao je da potiče razmnožavanje. Danas je, kaže, spolni odnos postao isključivo sredstvo užitka, a čovjek koristi svoje i tuđe tijelo za zadovoljenje dopaminskih potreba i nagona.

Korijen problema vidi u trenutku kad je žena odvojena od "najljepše dimenzije svoje ženstvenosti", odnosno od majčinstva. Kao posljedicu navodi tvrdnju da je ubijanje nerođenog djeteta svake godine glavni uzrok smrti u svijetu. Majku koja u tome sudjeluje vidi i kao žrtvu tog procesa.
sections.subtitle_en: The split between sexuality and reproduction as a precedent in biological history
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet as a biologist speaks about the split of sexuality from reproduction
sections.content_en:
Josipa Nemet continues on the host's thought: society is most easily changed through children, that is, through norms that are inscribed into their neurobiology, especially through sexual morality. She sees the current state as an inevitable consequence of the "huge split" that occurred about fifty years ago.

As a biologist, she calls this split a **precedent** in the 4.5 billion-year-long history of life. A being has appeared, she says, that considers that it is not good to reproduce, and ultimately a being that no longer thinks it is good to live. She illustrates this with an example: cells do not have consciousness, but they always fight for life. Even in a person who tries to take his own life, she says, "all of his cells disagree with him". With this she explains the large number of failed suicide attempts.

Biology, she explains, strives for survival until reproduction. Man as a conscious being in addition to that has a higher dimension: he freely decides to love another person. Still, the patterns are deeply inscribed in the body. She describes the relationship between male and female as a "very fine and sensitive regulation of balance". Male and female gametes have existed for almost two billion years and have always coevolved, so every change in one sex demanded a complementary change in the other. All those changes led to union and the creation of life.

Opposite that history stands "a miserable 50 years", to which biology cannot adapt. First, sexuality was separated from reproduction, and then pleasure, which is evolutionarily younger, about five hundred million years old, and arose to encourage reproduction. Today, she says, sexual intercourse has become exclusively a means of pleasure, and man uses his own and another's body to satisfy dopamine needs and drives.

She sees the root of the problem in the moment when woman was separated from "the most beautiful dimension of her femininity", that is, from motherhood. As a consequence, she cites the claim that the killing of the unborn child every year is the leading cause of death in the world. She sees the mother who participates in this also as a victim of that process.

sections.subtitle: Što molekularni biolog ima sa zdravstvenim odgojem: kritika psihologije
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća kritizira modernu psihologiju zbog zanemarivanja biologije
sections.content:
Voditelj spominje kritiku na koju je naišao pri pripremi: što molekularni biolog ima s temom zdravstvenog odgoja? Smatra da je gošća u dotadašnjem razgovoru dala "pregršt argumenata" zašto se time može baviti i ona i svaki čovjek.

Josipa Nemet ponavlja misao iz uvodnog isječka. Moderna psihologija degradirala se jer je zanemarila da je ljudsko tijelo drevno i nosi određene obrasce. Zato ju je oduševilo što studij psihologije na **Hrvatskom katoličkom sveučilištu** ima predmet evolucijska psihologija. Čovjeka se, kaže, ne može razumjeti bez povijesti koju njegovo tijelo nosi "do trenutka kad je Gospodin udahnuo ljudsku dušu". Ni sociologija ni psihologija ne mogu se promatrati izvan okvira biologije.

Zbog toga su stručnjaci, prema njezinim riječima, zbunjeni porastom anksioznosti i suicidalnosti. Ona korijen toga vidi u iskoraku društva od onoga što je duboko u čovjeku. Spominje i **Jungove arhetipe** te priče i mitove kojima se to prenosilo. Kad se društvo udalji od tih intrinzičnih struktura, dolazi do dezintegracije i destabilizacije osobe. Terapije koje se svode na to da se osoba dobro osjeća smatra promašenima jer osjećaji nisu glavni pojam u psihoterapiji. Dodaje da ne želi ulaziti u tuđu struku jer bi to bilo neprofesionalno, ali kao evolucijska biologinja vidi "veliko neznanje".

Najviše ju je šokiralo, kaže, kad je proučila predmete na studiju psihologije: biologije ima vrlo malo, a ozbiljne neurobiologije gotovo nimalo. Jednoj je kolegici objasnila da ta znanja "nisu ušla u sustav obrazovanja". Prema njezinim riječima, studenti barataju razinom biologije koju njezina kći već zna u prvom razredu srednje škole. Roditelji čija djeca studiraju psihologiju u Rijeci poslali su joj prezentaciju s predavanja vezanog uz biologiju. Ocjenjuje je "tragičnom" i "infiltriranom ideologijom" koja ne stvara stručnjake nego ideološke aktiviste.

Gošća poziva državu da zaštiti obrazovni sustav. Podsjeća da su hrvatski stručnjaci u svijetu bili cijenjeni i lako dobivali postdoktorska mjesta. Posljedice vidi već danas: djeca s identitetskim problemima dolaze kod psihologa koje je, kako kaže, "odgojila ideologija na Filozofskom fakultetu".
sections.subtitle_en: What a molecular biologist has to do with health education: a critique of psychology
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest criticizes modern psychology for neglecting biology
sections.content_en:
The host mentions a criticism he encountered during preparation: what does a molecular biologist have to do with the topic of health education? He considers that the guest, in the conversation up to that point, provided a "handful of arguments" as to why both she and every person can deal with it.

Josipa Nemet repeats the thought from the introductory clip. Modern psychology has degraded because it neglected that the human body is ancient and carries certain patterns. That is why she was thrilled that the study of psychology at **Hrvatsko katoličko sveučilište** has an evolutionary psychology course. Man, she says, cannot be understood without the history his body carries "up to the moment when the Lord breathed in the human soul." Neither sociology nor psychology can be observed outside the framework of biology.

Because of this, according to her words, experts are confused by the rise in anxiety and suicidality. She sees the root of this in society stepping away from what is deep within man. She also mentions **Jung's archetypes** and the stories and myths through which this was transmitted. When society moves away from these intrinsic structures, the disintegration and destabilization of the person occurs. She considers therapies that boil down to a person feeling good to be failures because feelings are not the main concept in psychotherapy. She adds that she does not want to enter someone else's profession because that would be unprofessional, but as an evolutionary biologist she sees "great ignorance."

What shocked her the most, she says, was when she studied the courses in the psychology program: there is very little biology, and almost no serious neurobiology. She explained to a colleague that this knowledge "did not enter the education system." According to her words, students operate with a level of biology that her daughter already knows in the first grade of high school. Parents whose children study psychology in Rijeka sent her a presentation from a lecture related to biology. She assesses it as "tragic" and "infiltrated with ideology" that does not produce experts, but ideological activists.

The guest calls on the state to protect the education system. She recalls that Croatian experts were valued in the world and easily obtained postdoctoral positions. She already sees the consequences today: children with identity problems come to psychologists whom, as she says, "ideology at Filozofski fakultet raised."

sections.subtitle: "Ovo nije sukob svjetonazora, nego borba protiv biologije"
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet govori o jednom jedinom znanstvenom radu u bibliografiji kurikuluma
sections.content:
Na voditeljevu opasku da znanstveni radovi zagovornicima kurikuluma "ne idu u prilog", Josipa Nemet odgovara da se ne radi o sukobu svjetonazora. Po njoj je to **borba protiv biologije**. S protivnicima ne želi razgovarati jezikom svjetonazora, nego jezikom znanosti. Tvrdi da oni to ne mogu jer od 40 milijuna znanstvenih radova iz medicine i biologije ne mogu naći nijedan koji bi poduprio njihove teze. Zato, kaže, uglavnom izbjegavaju rasprave.

U bibliografiji kurikuluma, prema njezinim riječima, nalazi se samo jedan znanstveni rad. Ostalo su naputci **Svjetske zdravstvene organizacije**, **Europske unije** i drugih tijela, u kojima također nema radova o neurobiologiji i dječjem razvoju. Taj jedini rad, kaže, analizirao je uspješnost sveobuhvatne seksualne edukacije i pokazao pozitivan učinak na znanje djece. Gošća to smatra trivijalnim: dijete će zapamtiti i ponoviti ono što mu se ponavlja. To, međutim, neće usmjeriti njegovo ponašanje kad mora odlučivati, zbog osjetljive neurobiologije i sklonosti riziku koja je u adolescenciji veća nego ikad u životu.

Iznosi i drugu mogućnost: možda idejni začetnici takvog pristupa sve to dobro znaju i zato žele što ranije doći do djece kako bi promijenili njihov normativni sustav. Produljeno djetinjstvo je, objašnjava, faza u kojoj zajednica uvodi nove članove u kulturu. Citira **Chestertona**, prema kojem se odgojem prenosi "sama duša kulture". Zato odgojitelje, pod čime misli na učitelje i roditelje, smatra najvažnijim osobama u društvu. Upozorava da će, ako se autoritet nad neurobiologijom djece u javnom sustavu prepusti ideolozima, društvo za dvadeset godina biti upravo onakvo kakvo danas samo bira.
sections.subtitle_en: "This is not a conflict of worldviews, but a struggle against biology"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet speaks about the one and only scientific paper in the curriculum's bibliography
sections.content_en:
To the host's remark that scientific papers "are not in favor" of the curriculum's advocates, Josipa Nemet responds that it is not about a conflict of worldviews. According to her, it is a **struggle against biology**. She does not want to talk to opponents in the language of worldviews, but in the language of science. She claims that they cannot do that because out of 40 million scientific papers in medicine and biology, they cannot find a single one that would support their theses. That is why, she says, they mostly avoid discussions.

In the curriculum's bibliography, according to her words, there is only one scientific paper. The rest are guidelines of the **World Health Organization**, the **European Union**, and other bodies, in which there are also no papers on neurobiology and child development. That single paper, she says, analyzed the effectiveness of comprehensive sexuality education and showed a positive effect on children's knowledge. The guest considers this trivial: a child will remember and repeat what is repeated to it. That, however, will not guide its behavior when it has to make decisions, because of sensitive neurobiology and a propensity for risk that is greater in adolescence than ever in life.

She also presents another possibility: perhaps the originators of such an approach know all this very well and therefore want to reach children as early as possible in order to change their normative system. Extended childhood is, she explains, a phase in which the community introduces new members into culture. She quotes **Chesterton**, according to whom upbringing transmits "the very soul of a culture". That is why she considers educators, by which she means teachers and parents, to be the most important people in society. She warns that, if authority over children's neurobiology in the public system is surrendered to ideologues, in twenty years society will be exactly what it chooses for itself today.

sections.subtitle: Niska sklonost strahu i "lakša opcija" djelovanja
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća objašnjava zašto je strah ne sputava u javnom angažmanu
sections.content:
Voditelj pita što je bio presudni "klik" da se uključi u **udrugu Članak 64** i javni angažman. Podsjeća da je ona viša asistentica na institutu i pita boji li se za radno mjesto ili obitelj. Kaže da poznaje ljude iz znanstvenog sustava koji se zbog posla, članaka i citiranosti ne žele javno izjasniti. Njega su, kaže, zbog stavova neki i "unfriendali".

Josipa Nemet odgovara da to ovisi o karakteru i osobinama ličnosti. Spominje **neurotičnost**, odnosno sklonost strahu, koja je u populaciji široko raspoređena. Dobro je za zajednicu da ima ljude na oba kraja tog spektra jer se odluke tako izbalansiraju. Za sebe kaže da ima "izrazito nisku" neurotičnost i da njome strah ne upravlja. Dodaje da bi joj možda bilo bolje da je bliže sredini. Žene, objašnjava, češće naginju neurotičnosti, pa u braku nastaje "lijepa vaga" pri donošenju odluka.

Oslonac vidi i u svojoj duhovnosti te se vodi **Sokratovom** mišlju da je jedino loše što se čovjeku može dogoditi ono što sam loše učini. Lošim smatra i propustiti učiniti dobro za društvo. Motivira je i velika ljubav prema djeci, ne samo svojoj, jer ih vidi kao stvorenja koja zaslužuju šansu.

U tom kontekstu spominje pojam "zarobljene savjesti" koji je koristio **papa Benedikt** te riječi **svetog Pavla** da "duh hoće, ali tijelo ne može". Sloboda, kaže, nije zadovoljavanje svakog nagona, nego sposobnost da se odluči što je dobro za sebe, za bližnjega i za zajednicu. Za sebe kaže da joj je teže promatrati i pasivno slušati "ružne priče" koje se nameću djeci nego djelovati. Uključivanje joj je zato, priznaje, "lakša opcija, a ne teža".
sections.subtitle_en: Low Propensity for Fear and the "Easier Option" of Action
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why fear does not hold her back in public engagement
sections.content_en:
The host asks what the decisive "click" was to get involved in the **association Članak 64** and public engagement. He recalls that she is a senior assistant at an institute and asks if she fears for her job or family. He says he knows people from the scientific system who, because of work, articles, and citations, do not want to speak out publicly. Some people, he says, have even "unfriended" him because of his views.

Josipa Nemet responds that this depends on character and personality traits. She mentions **neuroticism**, that is, the propensity for fear, which is widely distributed in the population. It is good for the community to have people on both ends of that spectrum because decisions are balanced that way. For herself, she says that she has "extremely low" neuroticism and that fear does not control her. She adds that it might be better for her to be closer to the middle. Women, she explains, tend toward neuroticism more often, so in marriage a "nice balance" is created when making decisions.

She also finds support in her spirituality and is guided by **Socrates'** thought that the only bad thing that can happen to a man is what he himself does badly. She also considers failing to do good for society to be bad. She is also motivated by a great love for children, not only her own, because she sees them as creatures who deserve a chance.

In that context, she mentions the concept of "captive conscience" used by **Pope Benedict**, and the words of **Saint Paul** that "the spirit wants, but the body cannot". Freedom, she says, is not satisfying every impulse, but the ability to decide what is good for oneself, for one's neighbor, and for the community. For herself, she says that it is harder for her to observe and passively listen to "ugly stories" being imposed on children than to act. Getting involved is therefore, she admits, the "easier option, not the harder one".

sections.subtitle: Od "Karata na stol" do udruge nazvane po ustavnom članku
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet objašnjava kako je inicijativa Karte na stol prerasla u udrugu Članak 64
sections.content:
Voditelj pita odakle ime udruge i što je dosad postignuto. Josipa Nemet objašnjava da su počeli kao inicijativa **Karte na stol**. Naziv je bio privlačan jer su tada bile aktualne "karte seksalice", pa su pozvali da se otvore i njihove i vlastite karte. Održan je i prosvjed. Kako se okupilo više ljudi, uključujući pravni i administrativni tim, zaključili su da je za djelovanje u društvu najjednostavnije osnovati udrugu.

Ime **Članak 64** dolazi od članka Ustava koji smatraju "zadnjom branom" zdravog i radosnog djetinjstva pred ideološkim pritiscima. Taj članak, objašnjava, roditeljima jamči pravo da donose konačnu odluku o odgoju svoje djece. Zakoni se mijenjaju lako i često "iza kulisa", pa se zaštita djece i prava roditelja postupno slabe. Ustav je krovni dokument koji se ne mijenja tako lako. Zato je, ističe, važno stalno se pozivati na to pravo, jer roditelj ima najveću ljubav prema djetetu i prirodni nagon da mu čini dobro kad dobije pravu informaciju.
sections.subtitle_en: From "Cards on the Table" to an Association Named After a Constitutional Article
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet explains how the initiative Karte na stol grew into the association Članak 64
sections.content_en:
The host asks where the name of the association comes from and what has been achieved so far. Josipa Nemet explains that they started as the initiative **Karte na stol**. The name was attractive because "sex cards" were topical at the time, so they called for both their cards and one's own cards to be laid on the table. A protest was also held. As more people gathered, including a legal and administrative team, they concluded that founding an association was the simplest way to act in society.

The name **Članak 64** comes from the article of the Constitution that they consider the "last bulwark" of a healthy and joyful childhood against ideological pressures. That article, she explains, guarantees parents the right to make the final decision about the upbringing of their children. Laws are changed easily and often "behind the scenes," so the protection of children and parents' rights are gradually weakened. The Constitution is an umbrella document that is not changed so easily. That is why, she emphasizes, it is important to constantly invoke that right, because a parent has the greatest love for the child and a natural instinct to do good to them when they receive the right information.

sections.subtitle: Web stranica sa znanstvenim sadržajem za roditelje
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća predstavlja web stranicu udruge sa znanstvenim člancima za roditelje
sections.content:
Glavni smjer djelovanja udruge, objašnjava Josipa Nemet, jest da "ne mogu djelovati mimo roditelja". Rade preko njih i računaju da će roditelj, kad dobije istinitu informaciju, dobro procijeniti i odlučiti za svoje dijete.

Uz društvene mreže odmah su počeli izrađivati **web stranicu**, na koju redovito dodaju:
- znanstvena istraživanja,
- stručne članke i analize o dječjem neurorazvoju,
- sadržaje o štetnosti ovisničkih obrazaca, osobito pornografije.

Cilj je da roditelji "crno na bijelo" pročitaju da je ono na što ih udruga upozorava znanstveno potvrđeno. Objavljuju i članke o događanjima u inozemstvu. Hrvatska, kaže, "srećom kasni" i u lošim stvarima. Vani se sveobuhvatna seksualna edukacija provodi već 15 do 20 godina, a današnje su verzije znatno ekstremnije od riječkih početaka. Stranica tako treba pokazati što nas čeka za deset ili dvadeset godina ako se ne reagira na vrijeme.
sections.subtitle_en: Website with scientific content for parents
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest presents the association's website with scientific articles for parents
sections.content_en:
The main direction of the association's activity, explains Josipa Nemet, is that they "cannot act bypassing parents". They work through them and count on the fact that a parent, once they receive truthful information, will assess well and decide for their child.

Along with social networks, they immediately began developing a **website**, to which they regularly add:
- scientific research,
- professional articles and analyses on child neurodevelopment,
- content on the harmfulness of addictive patterns, especially pornography.

The goal is for parents to read "in black and white" that what the association is warning them about is scientifically confirmed. They also publish articles about events abroad. Croatia, she says, is "fortunately lagging behind" in bad things as well. Abroad, comprehensive sexuality education has already been implemented for 15 to 20 years, and today's versions are considerably more extreme than the Rijeka beginnings. The website should thus show what awaits us in ten or twenty years if action is not taken in time.

sections.subtitle: Francuska: obvezni program od treće godine i otežano školovanje kod kuće
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet opisuje iskustva francuskih roditelja s nacionalnim kurikulumom spolnog odgoja
sections.content:
Josipa Nemet spominje konferenciju na koju su pozvani roditelji iz **Francuske**, gdje je, kako kaže, program došao "do krajnjih granica". Francuski nacionalni kurikulum naziva "degutantnim" i ističe da je obvezan i u katoličkim školama. Zato je hrvatska retorika o povlačenju djece iz programa za francuske prilike nedostatna.

Francuski su roditelji počeli školovati djecu kod kuće, ali je država, kaže, i to maksimalno ograničila. Za razliku od Amerike, gdje je dovoljno reći "hoću homeschoolati", u Francuskoj roditelji moraju predati opsežnu dokumentaciju i dokazati objektivan razlog, najčešće zdravstveni.

Spolni odgoj ondje traje od treće do 16. godine, a dobna granica stalno se spuštala. Najprije se smatralo da je srednja škola prekasno jer učenici već imaju ugrađene moralne obrasce. Zatim se prigovaralo da djeca u prvi razred dolaze s već razvijenom "heteronormativnošću i cisnormativnošću". Gošća to ironično komentira: djeca imaju majku i oca, pa ih to "valjda navodi" na takvo shvaćanje. Prema njezinim riječima, u većini tih zemalja djeca od treće godine dolaze "na indoktrinaciju", dva do tri puta mjesečno moraju biti odjevena kao suprotni spol i već tada slušaju o različitim rodnim identitetima. Svjesna je da to prosječnom Hrvatu zvuči nadrealno.
sections.subtitle_en: France: mandatory program from the age of three and restricted homeschooling
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet describes the experiences of French parents with the national sex education curriculum
sections.content_en:
Josipa Nemet mentions a conference to which parents from **France** were invited, where, as she says, the program reached "the extreme limits". She calls the French national curriculum "disgusting" and points out that it is mandatory in Catholic schools as well. That is why the Croatian rhetoric about withdrawing children from the program is insufficient for French circumstances.

French parents began homeschooling their children, but the state, she says, restricted that to the maximum as well. Unlike America, where it is enough to say "I want to homeschool", in France parents must submit extensive documentation and prove an objective reason, most often health-related.

Sex education there lasts from the age of three to 16, and the age limit has constantly been lowered. At first, high school was considered too late because students already have built-in moral patterns. Then complaints were made that children arrive in the first grade with already developed "heteronormativity and cisnormativity". The guest comments on this ironically: children have a mother and a father, so that "presumably leads" them to such an understanding. According to her words, in most of those countries children from the age of three come "for indoctrination", two to three times a month they must be dressed as the opposite sex, and already then they listen about different gender identities. She is aware that this sounds surreal to the average Croat.

sections.subtitle: Obitelji koje se iz Njemačke vraćaju zbog ideološkog sadržaja
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o obiteljima koje se vraćaju iz Njemačke, a voditelj nadovezuje svoja saznanja
sections.content:
Da to nije nadrealno, Josipa Nemet potkrepljuje primjerom: u posljednja dva mjeseca saznala je za pet ili šest obitelji koje se iz **Njemačke** vraćaju isključivo zbog izloženosti djece ekstremnom ideološkom i seksualiziranom sadržaju u vrtiću ili školi. "To je naša stvarnost", kaže. Zadaća je, prema njezinim riječima, pobrinuti se da mjesto u koje se te obitelji vraćaju za deset godina ne postane isto onome od čega su pobjegle.

Voditelj dodaje da je i sam čuo za takve programe u Njemačkoj. Roditelji ondje djecu ispisuju na tjedan ili dva dok sporni sadržaj ne prođe, a zatim ih vraćaju u školu. Ocjenjuje da ni to nije sretno rješenje i da rad gošće i njezine udruge treba podržati.
sections.subtitle_en: Families returning from Germany because of ideological content
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about families returning from Germany, and the host adds his own insights
sections.content_en:
That this is not surreal, Josipa Nemet substantiates with an example: in the last two months she has learned of five or six families who are returning from **Germany** exclusively due to the exposure of children to extreme ideological and sexualized content in kindergarten or school. "That is our reality," she says. The task, according to her words, is to make sure that the place to which these families return does not in ten years become identical to what they fled from.

The host adds that he himself has heard of such programs in Germany. Parents there unenroll their children for a week or two until the controversial content passes, and then return them to school. He assesses that this is not a fortunate solution either and that the work of the guest and her association should be supported.

sections.subtitle: Bitka za djetinjstvo počinje kod kuće: kriza djetinjstva zapravo je kriza roditeljstva
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet objašnjava da je današnja kriza djetinjstva prvenstveno kriza roditeljstva
sections.content:
Na početku drugog dijela razgovora voditelj se nadovezuje na priče o njemačkim programima spolnog odgoja. Ondje, kako je čuo, roditelji ispisuju djecu iz nastave na tjedan ili dva dok sporni sadržaji ne prođu. Takvo rješenje ne smatra najsretnijim, ali ističe da rad udruge zaslužuje podršku. Zatim razgovor širi izvan teme seksualizacije. Spominje konferenciju **Bitka za djetinjstvo** u organizaciji udruge Članak 64 i pita kakva se još bitka vodi za djecu, osim one u obrazovnom sustavu.

Dr. sc. Josipa Nemet odgovara da je srž te bitke činjenica da se dijete **prerano gura iz djetinjstva u odraslost**. To se ne događa samo kroz školski sustav, nego kroz cijeli javni prostor, od jumbo plakata do televizijskih serija. Ipak, ključni problem vidi drugdje: roditeljstvo se, kaže, jako promijenilo. Njezina je teza jasna: **današnja kriza djetinjstva prvenstveno je kriza roditeljstva.**

Tehnologija koja utječe na djecu jednako snažno utječe i na roditelje, a to je, prema njezinim riječima, na nevjerojatan način promijenilo odgoj. Dijete od najranije dobi treba prisutnost roditelja, a nedostaje već i fizička prisutnost jer djeca s godinu dana idu u jaslice. Taj podatak Nemet naziva „doslovno tragedijom“ i tvrdi da ne postoji znanstveno ni biološko utemeljenje po kojemu bi to bilo dobro za dijete.

No djetetu nije dovoljna samo fizička prisutnost. Nedostaje mu, kako kaže, **roditeljski pogled**, jer „dijete se sluša očima“. Svaka majka može posvjedočiti da joj dijete, dok nešto priča, stalno okreće glavu prema sebi. Roditelji, smatra Nemet, nisu svjesni koliko ta pozornost znači za razvoj dječje neurobiologije i za njegovo urastanje u zdrav identitet. Dijete identitet gradi prvenstveno kroz **osnovni relacijski trokut: majku, oca i sebe**. Taj odnos je „priručnik“ koji dijete čita i kroz koji gleda vlastiti život. Promjene u posljednjih 20 do 30 godina, zaključuje, na djeci se itekako vide.
sections.subtitle_en: The battle for childhood begins at home: the crisis of childhood is actually a crisis of parenting
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet explains that today's crisis of childhood is primarily a crisis of parenting
sections.content_en:
At the beginning of the second part of the conversation, the host follows up on stories about German sex education programs. There, as he heard, parents withdraw their children from classes for a week or two until the controversial content passes. He does not consider such a solution the most fortunate, but emphasizes that the association's work deserves support. Then he expands the conversation beyond the topic of sexualization. He mentions the conference **Bitka za djetinjstvo** organized by the association Članak 64 and asks what other battle is being fought for children, besides the one in the educational system.

Dr. sc. Josipa Nemet replies that the core of that battle is the fact that a child **is pushed too early from childhood into adulthood**. This does not happen only through the school system, but through the entire public space, from billboards to television series. Nevertheless, she sees the key problem elsewhere: parenting, she says, has changed greatly. Her thesis is clear: **today's crisis of childhood is primarily a crisis of parenting.**

Technology that affects children affects parents just as strongly, and that, according to her words, has changed upbringing in an incredible way. From the earliest age, a child needs the presence of parents, and already even physical presence is lacking because children go to nursery at one year of age. Nemet calls this fact "literally a tragedy" and claims that there is no scientific or biological foundation according to which this would be good for a child.

Yet physical presence alone is not enough for a child. What it is missing, as she says, is the **parental gaze**, because "a child is listened to with the eyes." Every mother can testify that while her child is talking about something, it constantly turns her head toward itself. Parents, Nemet believes, are not aware of how much this attention means for the development of the child's neurobiology and for its growth into a healthy identity. A child builds identity primarily through the **basic relational triangle: mother, father, and itself**. That relationship is the "handbook" that the child reads and through which it looks at its own life. The changes over the last 20 to 30 years, she concludes, are very much visible in children.

sections.subtitle: Zanemarujući i permisivni odgoj kao istoznačnice: zašto djeci treba „odgoj za žrtvu“
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća govori o odgoju za žrtvu i važnosti odgode trenutnog užitka
sections.content:
Josipa Nemet zatim imenuje obrazac koji smatra najraširenijim: **zanemarujući odgoj**. Dodaje da danas ne vidi razliku između zanemarujućeg i permisivnog odgoja jer su joj to, kako kaže, istoznačnice. Roditelji su, objašnjava, prestali odgajati svjesno i počeli **instantno ugađati svakoj dječjoj potrebi i svakom nagonu**.

Opasnost vidi u tome što se djecu tako sprječava u onome što naziva **odgojem za žrtvu**. Cijeli ljudski život, tumači, traži žrtvu ako se želi stvoriti nešto kvalitetno. Čovjek mora odgoditi trenutni užitak zbog nečega dobrog u budućnosti. Upravo zato su ljudi, za razliku od životinja, bića koja mogu predviđati i planirati.

Tu se Nemet poziva na pojam **„dovoljno dobre majke i oca“**: roditelja koji djetetu omogućuju razdoblja blage frustracije. Između „želim“ i „imam“ mora postojati odmak. Taj odmak nije samo odgojna, nego i neurobiološka kategorija:

- u tom prostoru stvaraju se **tanke regulacijske sinapse**;
- ponavljanjem odgojnih metoda one se utvrđuju i podebljavaju;
- s vremenom ih dijete **internalizira**, pa mu kao zrelom više ne treba vanjska modulacija roditelja.

Zaključak gošće je da u današnjem odgoju izrazito nedostaje frustracije. Voditelj dodaje da nedostaje i granica kod roditelja, s čime se gošća odmah slaže.
sections.subtitle_en: Neglectful and permissive parenting as synonyms: why children need "upbringing for sacrifice"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about upbringing for sacrifice and the importance of delaying immediate pleasure
sections.content_en:
Josipa Nemet then names the pattern she considers most widespread: **neglectful parenting**. She adds that today she does not see a difference between neglectful and permissive parenting because to her, as she says, they are synonyms. Parents, she explains, have stopped raising children consciously and have begun **instantly catering to every child's need and every impulse**.

She sees the danger in the fact that children are thus prevented from what she calls **upbringing for sacrifice**. The whole of human life, she explains, demands sacrifice if one wants to create something of quality. A person must delay immediate pleasure for the sake of something good in the future. That is precisely why humans, unlike animals, are beings who can foresee and plan.

Here Nemet refers to the concept of **"a good enough mother and father"**: parents who allow the child periods of mild frustration. Between "I want" and "I have" there must be a distance. That distance is not only an educational, but also a neurobiological category:

- in that space, **thin regulatory synapses** are formed;
- by repeating parenting methods, they are established and thickened;
- over time, the child **internalizes** them, so as a mature person they no longer need external modulation from the parents.

The guest's conclusion is that in today's upbringing, frustration is distinctly lacking. The host adds that boundaries among parents are also lacking, with which the guest immediately agrees.

sections.subtitle: Ograđeni vrt, blagodat dosade i sjećanje na žeđ s košarkaškog igrališta
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet objašnjava zašto su dosada i igra temelj dječje samoregulacije
sections.content:
Granice, objašnjava Josipa Nemet, djetetu daju sigurnost. Uspoređuje ih s **ograđenim vrtom** u kojemu dijete ima svu slobodu, ali vrt mora imati ogradu, jer je dijete bez nje frustrirano. Kad mu se daje autonomija, dijete ne zna što bi s njom. Njegova biologija još nema dijelove mozga koji tom autonomijom mogu upravljati. Autonomiju će rado prihvatiti, ali će je iskoristiti preko **nagradnog sustava**: stvarat će si užitak, igrati igrice „bjesomučno“, prejedati se ili tražiti stalnu validaciju na društvenim mrežama. To posljednje, napominje, podiže dopamin, osobito kod djevojčica.

Najopasnijim smatra **izostanak dosade**. Dosada je, prema njoj, najvažniji oblik frustracije za dijete jer ga potiče da stvara i da se igra. Zato je **igra najkvalitetniji oblik stimulacije nagradnog sustava**. U igri s drugima dijete se mora prilagoditi i pričekati jer je netko drugi prvi uzeo igračku. Mali „šutevi dopamina“, potrebni za motivaciju, isprekidani su čekanjem. Upravo iz toga nastaju regulacija i sposobnost samokontrole.

Danas, upozorava, djeca ne samo da nemaju dosade, nego dobivaju jesti prije nego što su gladna i piti prije nego što su žedna. Kao primjer navodi prijateljice koje djecu stalno šalju da popiju vode, iako će se dijete samo napiti kad ožedni. Usporedbe radi, prisjeća se vlastitog djetinjstva. Igrala je košarku, nije bilo boca s vodom kakve danas svi nose, a do vodoskoka vani nije joj se dalo ići. Djeca su tada znala što su žeđ i glad, a važnije im je bilo pucati na koš nego odmah piti.

Takve situacije Nemet naziva važnim neurobiološkim događajima za razvoj samokontrole. One u konačnici razvijaju i sposobnost da se čovjek jednog dana **žrtvuje**, ne samo za vlastito dobro, nego i za dobro osobe koja mu je važna. Zato se, zaključuje, ne treba čuditi što je danas toliko ljudi koji se za drugoga ne žele žrtvovati.
sections.subtitle_en: A fenced garden, the blessing of boredom, and the memory of thirst from the basketball court
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet explains why boredom and play are the foundation of children's self-regulation
sections.content_en:
Boundaries, explains Josipa Nemet, give a child security. She compares them to a **fenced garden** in which a child has all the freedom, but the garden must have a fence, because without it, the child is frustrated. When given autonomy, the child does not know what to do with it. Its biology does not yet have the parts of the brain that can manage that autonomy. It will gladly accept autonomy, but will utilize it through the **reward system**: it will create pleasure for itself, play games "frantically", overeat, or seek constant validation on social networks. The latter, she notes, raises dopamine, especially in girls.

She considers the **absence of boredom** to be the most dangerous. Boredom is, according to her, the most important form of frustration for a child because it encourages it to create and to play. That is why **play is the highest quality form of stimulation of the reward system**. In play with others, a child must adapt and wait because someone else took the toy first. Small "shots of dopamine", needed for motivation, are interrupted by waiting. It is precisely from this that regulation and the capacity for self-control arise.

Today, she warns, children not only lack boredom, but they get to eat before they are hungry and to drink before they are thirsty. As an example, she mentions female friends who constantly send their children to drink water, even though a child will drink on its own when it gets thirsty. For comparison, she recalls her own childhood. She played basketball, there were no water bottles like everyone carries today, and she did not feel like going outside to the water fountain. Children back then knew what thirst and hunger were, and it was more important to them to shoot at the basket than to drink right away.

Nemet calls such situations important neurobiological events for the development of self-control. In the end, they also develop the ability for a person to one day **sacrifice**, not only for one's own good, but also for the good of a person who is important to them. Therefore, she concludes, one should not wonder why today there are so many people who do not want to sacrifice for another.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija iz Japana: ni besplatni spojevi ne pomažu kad se izgubi smisao majčinstva
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća navodi primjer Japana i neuspjeh demografskih mjera
sections.content:
Kao krajnju posljedicu odgoja bez žrtve Josipa Nemet navodi **Japan**. Ondje ljudi, kaže, ne žele ulaziti u brakove, pa ni u veze, jer ih doživljavaju kao nepotrebnu smetnju koja traži odricanje. Roditelji koji su se odlučili na djecu ondje su, prema njezinim riječima, „povlaštena skupina“.

S tim primjerom kritizira i domaći demografski pristup koji se svodi na olakšice. Japanci imaju gotovo sve besplatno, od sportskih aktivnosti nadalje, a država daje čak i **bonove za odlazak na spoj**. Unatoč tome ljude ne uspijeva potaknuti ni na veze ni na brak, a kamoli na djecu. Problem je, zaključuje, negdje drugdje: djeca se više ne odgajaju **za majčinstvo i očinstvo**.

Nekada je to bilo nagonski: djevojčica je od rođenja gledala svoju majku. Nemet poručuje majkama da paze što govore pred djecom. Ne treba verbalno veličati majčinstvo, ali ne treba ni pred djecom prepričavati traume s poroda i neprestano govoriti koliko je sve teško. Ženi je, smatra, teško jer su joj nametnute uloge koje biološki ne može nositi istodobno. Uz to ju se uvjerilo da je važnije „na traci micati čepove“ nego stvarati „nova vječna bića“. To naziva **laži i varkom nametnutom ženi**: da vrijedi manje ako se posveti novom životu nego ako je „rob na blagajni ili na traci“.

Gošća naglašava da obrazovanje smatra važnim jer je i sama doktorica znanosti. Ipak, nitko je ne može uvjeriti da je jedan dan njezina rada ili jedno slovo znanstvenog rada važnije od toga da zakasni po dijete u vrtić. To je, kaže, bilo jasno svakom njezinom poslodavcu. Prisjeća se i čuđenja okoline kad je odlučila tri godine ostati kod kuće s djetetom: „Zar ćeš ti to napraviti?“ Takvo razmišljanje pripisuje društvu u koje su ljudi urasli. Oni ne shvaćaju da to nije odricanje, nego **izbor boljega**.
sections.subtitle_en: A lesson from Japan: not even free dates help when the meaning of motherhood is lost
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest cites the example of Japan and the failure of demographic measures
sections.content_en:
As the ultimate consequence of an upbringing without sacrifice, Josipa Nemet cites **Japan**. There, she says, people do not want to enter into marriages, or even into relationships, because they perceive them as an unnecessary hindrance that demands sacrifice. Parents who decided to have children there are, according to her words, a "privileged group".

With that example, she also criticizes the domestic demographic approach that comes down to benefits. The Japanese have almost everything for free, from sports activities onward, and the state even gives **vouchers for going on a date**. Despite this, it fails to encourage people either into relationships or into marriage, let alone into having children. The problem is, she concludes, somewhere else: children are no longer being raised **for motherhood and fatherhood**.

Once, this was instinctual: a girl watched her mother from birth. Nemet tells mothers to watch what they say in front of children. Motherhood does not need to be verbally glorified, but nor should traumas from childbirth be recounted in front of children and constantly talking about how difficult everything is. For a woman, she believes, it is difficult because roles have been imposed on her that she biologically cannot carry at the same time. In addition, she has been convinced that it is more important to "move caps on the line" than to create "new eternal beings". She calls this **a lie and a deception imposed on woman**: that she is worth less if she devotes herself to new life than if she is a "slave at the cash register or on the assembly line".

The guest emphasizes that she considers education important because she herself is a doctor of science. Still, no one can convince her that one day of her work or one letter of a scientific paper is more important than being late to pick up her child from kindergarten. That, she says, was clear to every one of her employers. She also recalls the astonishment of those around her when she decided to stay home with her child for three years: "Are you really going to do that?" She attributes such thinking to the society into which people have grown. They do not realize that this is not sacrifice, but **the choice of the better**.

sections.subtitle: Zbunjeni roditelji i pogrešni savjeti: zašto bebu ne treba ostaviti da se isplače
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet govori o pogrešnim savjetima stručnjaka i trajnim posljedicama na razini gena
sections.content:
Najviše joj je, kaže Josipa Nemet, žao same djece, jer su im **roditelji zbunjeni**. Zbunili su ih „raznorazni stručnjaci“ koji su posljednjih 20 do 30 godina davali dvojbene savjete. Kao primjer navodi raširenu tvrdnju da je dijete dobro **ostaviti da se isplače** umjesto da ga se utješi.

Desetljećima kasnije, ističe, znanstvena istraživanja pokazala su posljedice takvog pristupa na najdubljoj razini, onoj gena. To se područje izravno tiče **transkripcije**, kojom se gošća i sama bavi. Prema njezinim riječima, dolazi do reorganizacija koje ostaju trajne kroz cijeli život. Takve osobe ostaju **hipersenzibilne i teško se nose sa stresom** jer ih kao bebe nitko nije mazio, njegovao i nosio. Zato se, kako slikovito kaže, „nisu popalili promotori“ koji su se trebali aktivirati.

U detalje ne ulazi, ali naglašava opće načelo: **što je raniji stadij neurorazvoja, to obrazac ide dublje** u djetetovu neurobiologiju i teže ga je kasnije reintegrirati.

Voditelj iz toga izvodi zaključak da se tako stvara kaos: roditelji se udaljavaju od djece, a država tada preuzima odgoj preko škola.
sections.subtitle_en: Confused parents and mistaken advice: why a baby should not be left to cry it out
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet speaks about mistaken advice from experts and permanent consequences at the gene level
sections.content_en:
Most of all, says Josipa Nemet, she feels sorry for the children themselves, because their **parents are confused**. They were confused by "various experts" who have given dubious advice over the last 20 to 30 years. As an example, she cites the widespread claim that it is good **to leave a child to cry it out** instead of comforting it.

Decades later, she points out, scientific research showed the consequences of such an approach at the deepest level, that of genes. This field directly concerns **transcription**, which the guest herself also deals with. According to her words, reorganizations occur that remain permanent throughout life. Such persons remain **hypersensitive and have a hard time dealing with stress** because, as babies, no one cuddled, nurtured, and carried them. Therefore, as she picturesquely says, "the promoters did not fire up" that were supposed to activate.

She does not go into details, but emphasizes a general principle: **the earlier the stage of neurodevelopment, the deeper the pattern goes** into the child's neurobiology and the harder it is to reintegrate it later.

The host draws the conclusion from this that chaos is created in this way: parents drift away from their children, and the state then takes over upbringing through schools.
