sections.subtitle: Prvi spolni odgoj odvija se u dnevnom boravku: kako se majka i otac odnose jedno prema drugome
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet objašnjava da je odnos majke i oca najvažniji spolni odgoj za dijete
sections.content:
S obzirom na to da je malo vremena ostalo, voditelj prelazi na pitanja koja smatra najvažnijima za gledatelje. Podsjeća da je Josipa Nemet **majka petero djece, četiri kćeri i jednog sina**, a ona potvrđuje da njezina najstarija kći ima 15 godina. Voditelj pita kako, kada i na koji način razgovarati s djecom o seksualnosti, razlikuje li se pristup prema spolu djeteta i kako se uključuje njezin suprug. Napominje da roditelji tu temu najčešće prepuštaju satu razrednika i drugima, iako bi to trebali činiti sami.

Gošća odgovara da najvažniji spolni odgoj počinje **još prije rođenja**. Dijete u maternici čuje majčin glas, njezinu nježnost, pa i očev glas. Temelj spolnog odgoja je **odnos majke i oca**, odnosno odnos muškog i ženskog u koji dijete urasta. Dijete promatra kako se roditelji jedno drugome obraćaju, kako se dodiruju i kako se dočekuju kad netko dođe kući. Tako tjelesni dodir povezuje s nečim lijepim, ugodnim i relacijskim. Pojam relacije još ne poznaje, ali vidi da dodir stvara zajedništvo između ljudi koje voli.

Roditelji se, nastavlja, često uplaše kad se posvađaju pred djetetom. Navodi slučaj roditelja koji su se nakon svađe išli ispričati djetetu. Njezin savjet bio je da su se trebali ispričati jedno drugome. Dijete je povrijeđeno zato što su roditelji povrijedili jedno drugo, pa se i njegova obnova događa kroz **pomirenje roditelja**. Dijete je vrlo plastično i otvoreno za obnovu, a pomirenje roditelja, kaže, obnovit će svaku ranu.

Djevojčica, objašnjava Nemet, gradi svoju ženstvenost gledajući majku koja voli svoju ženstvenost i uživa u njezinoj ljepoti i nježnosti. U ocu istodobno vidi zaštitu i snagu: tata je heroj, „najjači na svijetu“, a majka tu sliku podržava. To je, prema njoj, presudno za duboke intrinzične strukture i zdrav neurobiološki razvoj. Druga strana to naziva **patrijarhatom**, na što gošća odgovara da je onda „valjda i sama biologija patrijarhalna“. Protivnici bi se s njom trebali boriti znanstvenim radovima, a ne na verbalnoj razini.
sections.subtitle_en: The first sex education takes place in the living room: how the mother and father treat each other
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet explains that the relationship between mother and father is the most important sex education for a child
sections.content_en:
Given that little time is left, the host moves on to the questions he considers most important for the viewers. He reminds that Josipa Nemet is **a mother of five children, four daughters and one son**, and she confirms that her oldest daughter is 15 years old. The host asks how, when, and in what way to talk with children about sexuality, whether the approach differs according to the sex of the child, and how her husband gets involved. He notes that parents most often leave that topic to the homeroom class and others, even though they should be doing it themselves.

The guest responds that the most important sex education begins **even before birth**. In the womb, the child hears the mother's voice, her tenderness, and even the father's voice. The foundation of sex education is **the relationship between mother and father**, that is, the relationship between male and female into which the child grows. The child observes how the parents address each other, how they touch each other, and how they welcome each other when someone comes home. Thus, the child connects physical touch with something beautiful, pleasant, and relational. The child does not yet know the concept of relation, but sees that touch creates communion between the people he or she loves.

Parents, she continues, are often frightened when they argue in front of the child. She mentions the case of parents who went to apologize to the child after an argument. Her advice was that they should have apologized to each other. The child is hurt because the parents hurt each other, so the child's renewal also happens through **the reconciliation of the parents**. The child is very plastic and open to renewal, and the reconciliation of the parents, she says, will renew every wound.

A girl, Nemet explains, builds her femininity by watching a mother who loves her femininity and enjoys its beauty and tenderness. At the same time, she sees protection and strength in the father: dad is a hero, "the strongest in the world," and the mother supports that image. According to her, that is crucial for deep intrinsic structures and healthy neurobiological development. The other side calls this **patriarchy**, to which the guest replies that then "biology itself is probably patriarchal too." Opponents should fight against her with scientific papers, and not on a verbal level.

sections.subtitle: Od potrebe za nježnošću do faze latencije: što roditelji trebaju znati o ranim fazama
sections.screenshot_description: Gošća opisuje ranodječju fazu, potrebu za nježnošću i fazu latencije
sections.content:
Dok je dijete malo, kaže Josipa Nemet, takav primjer roditelja je dovoljan i ništa drugo ne treba. Malo dijete svoje potrebe u velikoj mjeri zadovoljava **dodirom i nježnošću**. Ako nježnosti nedostaje, dijete je može tražiti samo, nadraživanjem dijelova tijela na kojima ima živčane završetke. Aktivisti to, napominje, nazivaju masturbacijom. Ona to opisuje kao **dječje nadraživanje** kojim dijete zadovoljava potrebu za nježnošću.

Savjet roditeljima je da djetetovu pažnju **preusmjere**, da ga uzmu, druže se s njim i maze ga. Tada se dijete „napije roditelja“ i te nježnosti, pa iz takvog ponašanja prirodno izraste. U određenoj dobi i samo instinktivno shvati da to ne radi pred drugima. Ključno je **ne napadati dijete** i ne stvoriti mu dojam da nešto nije u redu s njegovim tijelom, jer ono osjeća samo ugodu. Česta je pogreška, kaže, što se roditelji tada šokiraju, iako je riječ o posve normalnom stadiju.

Slijedi **faza latencije** u kojoj se gubi interes za tu tjelesnu ugodu. To je, ističe, vrlo važno razdoblje predadolescencije. Dijete se prirodno okreće prema van: prema zajednici, učenju i stjecanju iskustva. U mozgu se događa „ogromna sinaptička eksplozija“, pa je dijete poput **spužve za kulturu**. Tada mu roditelji polako mogu prenositi osnove.

Najbolje je, savjetuje, pričekati da dijete samo postavi pitanja. Hoće li ih postaviti, ovisi o tome ima li prisan odnos s roditeljem i je li tema stigmatizirana. Odgovori moraju biti prilagođeni dobi. Roditelji se mogu i sami educirati iz „predivnih knjiga“ o razgovoru s djecom o seksualnosti, a udruga, dodaje gošća, organizira i **radionice o tome kako s djecom razgovarati o spolnosti**.
sections.subtitle_en: From the need for tenderness to the latency stage: what parents need to know about the early stages
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the early childhood stage, the need for tenderness, and the latency stage
sections.content_en:
While a child is small, says Josipa Nemet, such an example of parents is sufficient and nothing else is needed. A small child satisfies its needs to a large extent through **touch and tenderness**. If tenderness is lacking, the child may seek it on its own, by stimulating parts of the body where it has nerve endings. Activists, she notes, call this masturbation. She describes it as **child stimulation** by which the child satisfies the need for tenderness.

The advice to parents is to **redirect** the child's attention, to take it, spend time with it, and cuddle it. Then the child "drinks its fill of the parents" and of that tenderness, so it naturally outgrows such behavior. At a certain age, it also instinctively understands not to do that in front of others. It is crucial **not to attack the child** and not to give it the impression that something is wrong with its body, because it only feels pleasure. It is a common mistake, she says, that parents get shocked then, even though it is a completely normal stage.

Next comes the **latency stage** in which interest in that bodily pleasure is lost. That is, she emphasizes, a very important period of pre-adolescence. The child naturally turns outward: toward the community, learning, and gaining experience. An "enormous synaptic explosion" happens in the brain, so the child is like a **sponge for culture**. Then parents can slowly pass on the basics to it.

It is best, she advises, to wait for the child to ask questions on its own. Whether it will ask them depends on whether it has a close relationship with the parent and whether the topic is stigmatized. The answers must be adapted to the age. Parents can also educate themselves from "wonderful books" on talking with children about sexuality, and the association, the guest adds, also organizes **workshops on how to talk to children about sexuality**.

sections.subtitle: Pubertet kao otkriće komplementarnosti i opasnost od devet minuta razgovora dnevno
sections.screenshot_description: Josipa Nemet upozorava na statistiku da roditelji s djecom razgovaraju svega 8 do 9 minuta
sections.content:
Kad se dijete približava spolnoj zrelosti, primjerice uz prvu menstruaciju, mora dobiti informacije o vlastitoj **fiziologiji**, objašnjava Josipa Nemet. Važno je, međutim, kako mu se te informacije prenose. Cilj je da se dijete, kako kaže, „zaljubi u to“, da vidi koliko je ljudsko tijelo lijepo i usklađeno.

To vrijedi i za djevojčice i za dječake. Usporedbom fizionomije dijete može uočiti **ljepotu komplementarnosti**: riječ je o jedinom sustavu koji je sam po sebi nedostatan, kojemu je potrebna druga osoba i koji svoju svrhu ostvaruje tek u zajedništvu s njom.

Iz toga gošća izvodi širu misao: **djeca se odgajaju kroz priče**, i kroz cijelu ljudsku povijest i danas. Djeca priče i traže. Problem je što se s njima više ne razgovara. Navodi „tragičnu statistiku“ prema kojoj roditelj s djetetom u prosjeku razgovara **8 do 9 minuta**, što naziva zastrašujućim. Bez narativa, priče i riječi, kaže, nema razvoja novog čovjeka.

Upozorenje je jasno: dijete će se, ako mu roditelji ne pričaju dobre priče, „ugraditi“ u **loše priče**. One ga fragmentiraju i neće ga izgraditi u odraslu osobu sposobnu stvarati nešto lijepo, živjeti za druge i doprinositi obitelji i zajednici.
sections.subtitle_en: Puberty as a discovery of complementarity and the danger of nine minutes of conversation a day
sections.screenshot_description_en: Josipa Nemet warns about the statistic that parents talk with their children for only 8 to 9 minutes
sections.content_en:
When a child approaches sexual maturity, for example with the first menstruation, they must receive information about their own **physiology**, explains Josipa Nemet. It is important, however, how this information is conveyed to them. The goal is for the child, as she says, to "fall in love with it", to see how beautiful and harmonized the human body is.

This applies to both girls and boys. By comparing physiognomy, a child can perceive the **beauty of complementarity**: it is the only system that is in itself insufficient, which needs another person, and which achieves its purpose only in communion with them.

From this, the guest draws a broader thought: **children are raised through stories**, both throughout all of human history and today. Children also seek stories. The problem is that people no longer talk to them. She cites a "tragic statistic" according to which a parent talks with a child on average for **8 to 9 minutes**, which she calls frightening. Without narrative, story, and words, she says, there is no development of a new human being.

The warning is clear: a child will, if parents do not tell them good stories, "embed itself" into **bad stories**. They fragment it and will not build it into an adult person capable of creating something beautiful, living for others, and contributing to family and community.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: puna kuća djece, heklanje, stroga pravila i svetost kao mjera uspjeha
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja blic pitanja, a gošća odgovara uz osmijeh
sections.content:
Voditelj priznaje da mu je žao prekidati razgovor i da bi se moglo još dugo razgovarati. Prije kraja ipak postavlja nekoliko blic pitanja tipa „ili-ili“, unaprijed upozoravajući da su neka „škakljiva“. Odgovori Josipe Nemet otkrivaju njezinu osobnost:

- **Znanstveni laboratorij ili puna kuća djece?** Bez oklijevanja: puna kuća djece. Voditelj komentira da je to bilo „ziher“.
- **Košarkaška utakmica ili mirna večera uz knjigu?** Sada već mirna večera uz knjigu. Gleda li se utakmicu, ne voli gledati, nego igrati. Da je izbor bio između heklanja i knjige, vjerojatno bi izabrala heklanje.
- **Roditeljski sastanak ili TV sučeljavanje?** Roditeljski sastanak, jer više voli susret s ljudima uživo nego sve „bestjelesno“. Ondje, kaže, ima i dobrih prijatelja.
- **Homeschooling ili potpuna reforma školstva?** Za njezinu obitelj i karaktere njezine djece bolja je škola, i to dobre škole.
- **Znanstveni rad ili javni aktivizam?** Velika snaga žene je u utjecaju, a s obzirom na svoj karakter smatra da je za društvo plodnija u javnom aktivizmu.
- **Stroga pravila ili potpuno povjerenje u djecu?** Stroga pravila, uz napomenu da su djeca tako sretnija. Voditelj dodaje: kad znaju granice.
- **Rasprava s ideološkim protivnikom ili pet sati dječjih tantruma?** Ni jedno ni drugo, a objektivna ne može biti jer joj tantrum nikad nije trajao toliko dugo i za to ima „svoje metode“. Ipak voli raspravljati s ideološkim protivnicima, ali na lijep način: kao natjecanje u razmišljanju, a ne debatu u kojoj se drugoga ponižava. U takvom razgovoru, smatra, oboje rastu.
- **Hrabro ili uspješno dijete?** Hrabro, ali uz protupitanje što znači uspjeh. Za nju je uspjeh da dijete bude **sveto**, a da bi postalo sveto, mora biti hrabro. Zato joj je pitanje „granično“. Voditelj primjećuje da je i za uspjeh potrebna hrabrost, pa je to povezano.

Gošća zaključuje da joj je jedini motiv za djecu da budu sveta. Voditelj dodaje da je to, po njegovu mišljenju, motiv svakog pravog katoličkog roditelja.
sections.subtitle_en: Quick-fire questions: a full house of children, crocheting, strict rules, and holiness as a measure of success
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks quick-fire questions, and the guest answers with a smile
sections.content_en:
The host admits that he is sorry to interrupt the conversation and that they could talk for much longer. Before the end, however, he asks a few quick-fire "either-or" questions, warning in advance that some are "tricky". Josipa Nemet's answers reveal her personality:

- **A scientific laboratory or a full house of children?** Without hesitation: a full house of children. The host comments that that was a "sure bet".
- **A basketball game or a quiet dinner with a book?** By now, a quiet dinner with a book. As for watching a game, she doesn't like to watch, but to play. If the choice had been between crocheting and a book, she probably would have chosen crocheting.
- **A parent-teacher meeting or a TV debate?** A parent-teacher meeting, because she prefers meeting people in person over anything "disembodied". There, she says, she also has good friends.
- **Homeschooling or a complete reform of the school system?** For her family and the characters of her children, school is better, specifically good schools.
- **Scientific work or public activism?** A woman's great power is in influence, and given her character, she considers that she is more fruitful for society in public activism.
- **Strict rules or complete trust in the children?** Strict rules, with the note that children are happier that way. The host adds: when they know the boundaries.
- **A discussion with an ideological opponent or five hours of children's tantrums?** Neither, and she cannot be objective because a tantrum has never lasted that long for her and she has "her own methods" for that. Still, she likes to discuss with ideological opponents, but in a nice way: as a competition in thinking, not a debate in which the other is humiliated. In such a conversation, she believes, both grow.
- **A brave or a successful child?** Brave, but with a counter-question about what success means. For her, success is for a child to be **holy**, and in order to become holy, it must be brave. That is why the question is "borderline" for her. The host observes that success also requires courage, so it is connected.

The guest concludes that her only motive for her children is for them to be holy. The host adds that this is, in his opinion, the motive of every true Catholic parent.

sections.subtitle: Zahvala gošći i najava: Dariova krunica među zatvorenicima
sections.screenshot_description: Isječak iz najave sljedeće epizode u kojemu Dario govori o molitvi s krunicom među zatvorenicima
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje Josipi Nemet na gostovanju i svemu što je izrekla te izražava nadu da će njezine riječi mnogima progovoriti. Najavljuje mogućnost još jedne zajedničke epizode jer je ostalo dovoljno materijala. Gošća odgovara da joj je bilo jako ugodno. Emisija se zatvara pozivom gledateljima da lajkaju i pretplate se te da podupru projekt i prate ga na **Patreonu**, gdje je sljedeća epizoda dostupna već danas.

Na samom kraju emitira se isječak iz sljedeće epizode. Sugovornik **Dario** govori o iskustvu iz zatvora u kojemu je s krunicom šetao među zatvorenicima, među kojima je katolika bilo malo, a mnogo Arapa i muslimana. Svakog od njih ujutro je javno blagoslivljao svetom vodom, „ne tajno“, i nitko mu nikada nije prigovorio.

Nakon petnaestak dana, prepričava Dario, svaki od zatvorenika počeo ga je moliti da se pomoli za ovo ili ono. Dok su oni kockali za stolom „kao u filmovima“, on je šetao s krunicom i molio za svakoga od njih. Tim molitvama, kaže, pristupao je odgovorno i nikada nije odbio nikoga tko ga je zamolio.
sections.subtitle_en: Thanks to the guest and announcement: Dario's Rosary among prisoners
sections.screenshot_description_en: Clip from the preview of the next episode in which Dario speaks about praying with the Rosary among prisoners
sections.content_en:
The host thanks Josipa Nemet for being a guest and for everything she expressed, and expresses hope that her words will speak to many. He announces the possibility of another joint episode because enough material remained. The guest replies that it was very pleasant for her. The show closes with an invitation to viewers to like and subscribe and to support the project and follow it on **Patreon**, where the next episode is already available today.

At the very end, a clip from the next episode is aired. The interlocutor **Dario** speaks about an experience from prison where he walked with a Rosary among prisoners, among whom there were few Catholics, and many Arabs and Muslims. Every morning he publicly blessed each of them with holy water, "not secretly", and no one ever objected.

After about fifteen days, Dario recounts, each of the prisoners began asking him to pray for this or that. While they gambled at the table "like in the movies", he walked with the Rosary and prayed for each of them. He approached these prayers, he says, responsibly and never turned down anyone who asked him.
